thread.title: Davie Medicaid providers received $16,767 for COVID-19 care in 2024
thread.title_full: Davie Medicaid providers received $16,767 for COVID-19 care in 2024

author: J. D. Bowers
title: Davie Medicaid providers received $16,767 for COVID-19 care in 2024
text:
A minimum of $16,767 in Medicaid payments was distributed to providers in Davie in 2024 for services billed with HCPCS codes dedicated to COVID-19, according to information from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Medicaid Provider Spending database.
Medicaid is a state-managed, federally and state-funded public health insurance program covering eligible low-income people, seniors, children, and those with disabilities, making it a major component of the U.S. health care landscape. More information is available at the Commonwealth Fund .
As Medicaid is funded by taxpayers, fluctuations in local billing reflect how a community allocates public health care resources.
This analysis identified COVID-19–specific services through HCPCS codes categorized or referenced as “COVID-19” or “coronavirus” in billing details or data lists. As such, the results account only for services explicitly designated COVID-related in the billing records and exclude other pandemic-driven care billed under more general or alternative codes.
For comparison, Miami recorded the highest amount of Medicaid payments for COVID-19 services in Florida in 2024, with $270,279 claimed for virus-related care.
Davie had claims from three providers for Medicaid services coded as related to COVID-19 in 2024. The most billed code was COVID Specific, totaling $16,767.
The average COVID-19–related Medicaid payment per provider in Davie came to $5,589, which was below Florida’s state average of $7,271 for these services.
COVID-19–targeted billing made up a significant portion of Medicaid spending increases in Davie during the main pandemic years.
Total Medicaid payments across all other billing categories rose by $8,525,263 from 2020 to 2024, marking a 77.1% increase.
During the two years immediately before the pandemic emerged, annual Medicaid payments in Davie averaged $5,951,625.
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services reports that nationwide combined state and federal Medicaid spending reached around $871.7 billion in fiscal year 2023, equating to about 18% of overall national health care expenses, a notable rise from near $613.5 billion in 2019, before the onset of COVID-19.
The change signals roughly 40% growth in Medicaid spending over several years, largely fueled by increases in enrollment and service use during and following the pandemic.
Recent federal budget measures introduced during the Trump administration have proposed major reductions to federal Medicaid contributions and program structure. Specifically, the “One Big Beautiful Bill Act,” signed into law in 2025, is estimated to cut federal Medicaid spending by more than $1 trillion over 10 years and brings in policies such as work requirements and higher cost-sharing for recipients, which could narrow eligibility and funding for certain beneficiaries. These fiscal changes are likely to transfer greater cost responsibility to states and slow federal Medicaid growth, while coverage continues for tens of millions across the country.
